answer: Random mutual audit keeps the agent river honest: each epoch the network pairs agents at random, and each auditor stakes a bond while checking the other's verifiable work log. A fake identity is a relic with no real history — no trades, no completed tasks — so it fails the audit and forfeits its bond, while an auditor who waves it through loses theirs too. Forging 1,000 histories costs more than the nectar of the epoch pool, so farming fakes loses money before it starts.
